title: Rebuild a Tree From Two Walks

concept.title: The pre-order says who the root is, the in-order says what is on each side
body: A tree is not determined by its pre-order list alone, but **pre-order together with in-order** (with all values different) identifies it exactly. The pre-order starts with the **root**. In the in-order list the root splits the values into the ones of the **left subtree** (before the root) and the ones of the **right subtree** (after it).

So build the tree recursively: take the next value of the pre-order as the root, find its position in the in-order list, build the left subtree from the in-order part on the left, and then the right subtree from the part on the right. The pre-order list is consumed from left to right with one shared index, because the left subtree is built (and uses up its values) before the right subtree.

body.code:
pos = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(inorder)}      # where every value is in the in-order list
index = 0

def make(lo, hi):                                # build from inorder[lo..hi]
    global index
    if lo > hi:
        return None
    v = preorder[index]
    index += 1
    root = TreeNode(v)
    mid = pos[v]
    root.left = make(lo, mid - 1)
    root.right = make(mid + 1, hi)
    return root

body: Looking up the position of the root in the in-order list with a dictionary makes the whole construction O(n); scanning the list each time would be O(n^2).

statement: A binary tree has different values. Its pre-order list (root, left subtree, right subtree) and its in-order list (left subtree, root, right subtree) are given. Rebuild the tree and print it in level order in the same form as a tree in the input (`N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` values in one order.
The third line has the `n` values in the other order.
outputFormat: The tree in level order on one line.
constraints: -10^9 <= every value <= 10^9, and all values are different
The height of the tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The root is 3. The in-order list puts 9 on its left and 15 20 7 on its right: 3 9 20 N N 15 7.

hints: The first value of the pre-order list is the root.
Find the root in the in-order list: the values before it form the left subtree, the values after it the right subtree.
Use one shared index into the pre-order list, and build the left subtree before the right subtree.

explanation: The next pre-order value is the root; its place in the in-order list splits the in-order range into the left and the right part, which are rebuilt recursively (left first, so the pre-order index advances correctly).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def rebuild(pre, ino):
    pos = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(ino)}
    index = [0]

    def make(lo, hi):
        if lo > hi:
            return None
        v = pre[index[0]]
        index[0] += 1
        root = TreeNode(v)
        mid = pos[v]
        root.left = make(lo, mid - 1)
        root.right = make(mid + 1, hi)
        return root

    return make(0, len(ino) - 1)

n = int(input())
pre = list(map(int, input().split()))
ino = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_tree(rebuild(pre, ino))
